elements.reason: Title explicitly includes 'Systematic Review'.

elements.quote: Effectiveness of Non-Pharmacological Interventions for Treating Post-Stroke Depressive Symptoms: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
elements.reason: Title specifies population (post-stroke depressive symptoms), intervention (non-pharmacological interventions), and study design (randomized controlled trials).

elements.quote: Effectiveness of Non-Pharmacological Interventions for Treating Post-Stroke Depressive Symptoms: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
elements.reason: Title includes supplementary information on analysis method (meta-analysis) and included study designs (randomized controlled trials).

elements.quote: With mixed conclusions, the effectiveness of pharmacological interventions for post-stroke depressive symptoms has not yet been determined. However, none of these reviews quantitatively demonstrated the effectiveness of different types of NPIs.
elements.reason: Describes current knowledge on interventions and important uncertainties regarding effectiveness and evidence gaps.

elements.quote: Therefore, to address this research gap, this study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis to synthesize and compare the available evidence regarding the effectiveness of various NPIs for treating depression in people following stroke.
elements.reason: Explains the importance and need for conducting the review to fill a research gap.

elements.quote: Three meta-analyses have been conducted to provide synthesized evidence on the effectiveness of pharmacological interventions for depressive symptoms following stroke, but results were mixed. Three reviews have identified several NPIs for post-stroke depression and have qualitatively provided evidence. However, none of these reviews quantitatively demonstrated the effectiveness of different types of NPIs.
elements.reason: Cites previous similar systematic reviews and explains the need for the current review due to mixed results and lack of quantitative synthesis.
No description of the proposed mechanism of action for the non-pharmacological interventions is provided in the retrieved evidence.
No evidence of logic model consideration in the rationale, and it may not apply as the review does not explicitly address complex interventions or delivery contexts in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: Objective: To compare the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions on depressive symptoms in people after stroke.
elements.reason: The objective is explicitly stated in the abstract using a comparative framework.

elements.quote: The PICOS (Participants, Interventions, Comparisons, Outcomes, Study Designs) checklist was used to identify the inclusion criteria in this review. Interventions (I) and controls (C): This review considered trials that compared the effects of NPIs for post-stroke individuals with depressive symptoms to control conditions.
elements.reason: Planned comparisons are explicitly stated using the PICOS framework.
